name: NMAT
conductingBody: Graduate Management Admission Council (GMAC), delivered by Graduate Management Global Connection (India) Private Limited (GMGC), a GMAC subsidiary
eligibility: GMAC sets no separate eligibility criterion for the test. Official terms: "It is the responsibility of the test taker to understand the eligibility requirements of all the universities and schools to which he/she is interested in applying before registering for the Test... test takers are advised to check the websites of each university and school where they plan to apply."
mode: Computer-adaptive test. Candidates located in India may take only the Test Centre Exam; candidates outside India may take only the Online Proctored Exam at Home.
frequency: Maximum of three attempts in a testing year (first attempt plus up to two retakes, No Shows included). A retake can be registered once the previous attempt's score has been received, for any date more than 15 days after the previous attempt. Each retake costs INR 3,000 (excluding taxes).

pattern.marking: Each section is scored 12-120; the total is 36-360. The three sections are weighted equally. There is no negative marking: no marks are deducted for wrong or unanswered questions.
pattern.notes: 108 multiple-choice questions in total. Before the test, there is a 2-minute NDA, an 8-minute tutorial and 3 minutes to choose section order. The test taker picks the order of the sections. Each section has its own time limit: unused time does not carry over, and you cannot return to a section once you leave it. GMAC's syllabus article gives 38 minutes for Language Skills; this file uses the 28 minutes stated in the official Terms and Conditions, which matches the 120-minute total.

syllabusAreas: Quantitative Skills: Number properties (fractions and decimals, logarithms, factors and multiples incl. LCM/HCF, prime numbers)
Quantitative Skills: Arithmetic (percentages, simple and compound interest, profit and loss, ratio, proportion and averages, time and work)
Quantitative Skills: Algebra and probability (linear and quadratic equations, inequalities, sequences and series, permutations and combinations, probability)
Quantitative Skills: Data interpretation and data sufficiency (caselets, graphs and charts, tables)
Logical Reasoning: Verbal reasoning (critical reasoning - conclusions, inferences, assumptions, strong/weak arguments, verbal logic; deductions)
Logical Reasoning: Analytical reasoning (syllogisms, analytical puzzles, input-output, seating arrangements, decision-making, Venn diagrams)
Language Skills: Reading comprehension, para forming, error identification, prepositions, sentence completion, analogies

registrationFee.category: Score sending to each additional school beyond the 5 included - India (excluding taxes)

scoreValidity: Valid for one application cycle only. GMAC: "your NMAT Exam score only lasts for one application cycle. If you want to apply with the NMAT again another year, you have to sit the NMAT again."

resultAndCounselling: Unofficial scores appear on screen right after the test. The official score card, with scaled section and total scores, is ready within 48 hours; exams flagged for security review are audited, and those results come out within 10 working days. Registration covers score sending to up to 5 programmes/schools, and each additional school costs extra. There is no central counselling. Each school runs its own admission process and NMAT cutoff, and GMAC says cutoffs vary by college and year.
